current.text: Isaiah Stewart is gone and Reed is Detroit's backup center.
Jalen Duren has signed with Detroit and is the projected starting center.
In the projected bench rotation, Isaiah Joe is the sixth man, followed by Ron Holland, Reed and Daniss Jenkins.
Duren's return limits his upside. If Duren plays about 28 minutes, Reed should play about 20.
If Duren misses time and Reed plays about 28 minutes, he could be a top 40 to 50 player. That makes him Detroit's stash option.
The newest preview still calls him a must-draft player in 14-team leagues, but now prefers him around round 13 instead of rounds 10 to 11. It calls his ESPN rank of 241 far too low.
Experts rate his play last season as excellent in both the regular season and the playoffs. They say he clearly outplayed Duren and Stewart, and the Pistons see him as better than Stewart.
For a season ending March 28, Detroit plays 4, 3 and 4 games in the fantasy playoff weeks. The team has 15 back-to-backs, and no rest risk is expected.

durable.text: He is an excellent per-minute producer.
He cannot carry the load of a 30-minute starter.
He has always posted high block rates per possession. 29% of his rim contests become blocks.
His value comes from efficient FG%, blocks, steals and few turnovers. He makes almost no threes and adds little in points and assists.

note: Both Yahoo and ESPN value him at 0 USD (ranks 165 and 241), and in a 144-player draft he is a 1 USD last-round stash at best. The newest expert price, round 13 in 14-team leagues, also puts him around the edge of our player pool. He fits punt 3PM builds that want FG%, blocks, steals and low turnovers from about 20 minutes off the bench. Early in the season, watch his minutes behind Duren and Duren's health: if Duren misses time, Reed becomes a must-add with top 50 upside.
